title: Quarterly scenario playbook: hosted API runway + model tiering to optimize cost/latency
creator: Lena Park
description: Objective: Produce a reproducible quarterly playbook that defines scenario-driven runway plans for the Hosted API and a pragmatic model-tiering strategy to meet OKRs for latency, cost-per-token, and availability. Background: customers expect stable latency and predictable pricing as new model variants are added. Current risk: ad-hoc model additions increase tail latency and raise unit cost without visibility. Scope: 1) Define three customer traffic scenarios (conversational low-latency, batch embeddings, high-throughput reranking). 2) For each scenario, prescribe: default hosted route, recommended model tier (latency vs cost tradeoffs), quantization/precision guidance, and auto-fallback targets. 3) Create canary rollout template and gating checklist tied to perf and quality metrics. 4) Produce an operational pruning schedule for legacy/low-usage variants. Deliverables: - Scenario matrix (CSV + one-pager) mapping routes to model tiers and expected P50/P95 latency and cost targets. - Canary rollout playbook with rollback triggers and telemetry queries. - Tiering policy spec (SLA labels: low-latency, balanced, cost-sensitive) and onboarding checklist for new models. - Example runtime config snippets for default batching/cache settings for each tier. Acceptance criteria: - Playbook reviewed and approved by Eng + Design + SRE. - Two hosted routes updated in staging with tiering policies and canary flow. - Observable dashboards with P50/P95 latency and token cost per route in Console. KPIs: reduce hosted API overall token cost by 9-12% for measured scenarios, maintain P95 latency <= target per scenario, decrease incident rate from model fallback by 30% for new model rollouts. Stakeholders: PM (Lena Park), Release Eng (Marco Delgado), Runtime Eng lead (Priya Shah), Design (Omar Ruiz), SRE (Akiko Tanaka). Risks & trade-offs: - Aggressive pruning may remove capability for niche workloads; mitigate with a slow deprecation window and migration guide. - Tiering increases operational surface area; mitigate with templated configs and runtime defaults. Timeline & milestones: Week 1: finalize scenarios and metrics. Week 2: prototype tier mappings + runtime config. Week 3: staging canary runs and dashboards. Week 4: review, docs, and staged rollout. Coordination: requires ENG sprint to add route-level labels and Console dashboard queries, and Design to approve UX for tier selection. Action items: 1) ENG to add telemetry hooks (ENG-28412). 2) Design to mock tier-picker UX (DES-1123). 3) PM to draft customer comms and migration FAQ. Links: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/hostedapi-scenario-playbook, GH RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/512, Dashboard proto: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/hostedapi-tiering
